definition: Margaret Mitchell is a computer scientist who works on algorithmic bias and fairness in machine learning.
details: She is best known for her work on automatically removing undesired biases concerning demographic groups from machine learning models, as well as more transparent reporting of their intended use.

explainer.lead: Margaret Mitchell (scientist) is an American computer scientist. Her work spans natural language processing, natural language generation and ethics of artificial intelligence.
explainer.knownFor: Notable works include On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots: Can Language Models Be Too Big? 🦜 and Model Cards for Model Reporting.

contributions.name: She enrolled in a PhD program at the University of Aberdeen, where she wrote a doctoral thesis on the topic of Generating Reference to Visible Objects, graduating in 2013.
Margaret Mitchell created the framework for recognizing and avoiding biases by testing with a variable for the group of interest, predictor and an adversary.

timeline.what: Mitchell obtained a bachelor's degree in linguistics from Reed College, Portland, Oregon, in 2005.
In 2012, Mitchell joined the Human Language Technology Center of Excellence at Johns Hopkins University as a postdoctoral researcher, before taking up a position at Microsoft Research in 2013.

In January 2021, after Timnit Gebru's termination from Google, Mitchell reportedly used a script to search through her corporate account and download emails that allegedly documented discriminatory incidents involving Gebru.
